title: The Geography of Algorithmic Judgment: LLM Intermediaries, Place Identity, and Racial Steering in Housing Search
abstract: arXiv:2606.06694v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are rapidly assuming an intermediary role in housing search through the integration of listing platforms within conversational interfaces, mediating access to information, search, and recommendations within urban settings. We expand on prior work on racial steering in LLMs by conducting a behavioral audit of seven open-weight and closed-source LLMs across four U.S. cities, testing location recommendations across three iterative prompting conditions that progressively add lifestyle preference context and reflect fair housing paired-testing methodologies. We find that steering is an emergent behavior of the model's interpretive license rather than primarily a static property. Steering results from the interaction of a user's identity, preference articulation, and the spatial logic that a model has internalized about learned representations of place, preference, and opportunity in a given city, and how

translated_title: 算法判断的地理学：大语言模型中介、地方身份与住房搜索中的种族引导
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）正通过将房源列表平台整合到对话式界面中，迅速承担起住房搜索中的中介角色，在城市环境中调解信息获取、搜索与推荐。我们在以往关于LLM种族引导研究的基础上，对美国四个城市的七个开放权重及闭源LLM进行了行为审计，在三种迭代提示条件下测试位置推荐，这些条件逐步加入生活方式偏好背景，并借鉴了公平住房配对测试的方法论。我们发现，种族引导主要是模型“解释许可”的一种涌现行为，而非一种静态属性。引导源于用户身份、偏好表达，以及模型对特定城市中地方、偏好与机会的学习表征所内化的空间逻辑这三者之间的交互作用。
tldr: 该论文通过对美国四个城市七个大语言模型的行为审计发现，住房搜索中的种族引导并非模型的静态属性，而是由用户身份、偏好表达方式与模型内化的城市空间逻辑交互作用所产生的涌现行为。
en_tdlr: Through a behavioral audit of seven open-weight and closed-source LLMs across four U.S. cities, this paper reveals that racial steering in housing search is an emergent behavior arising from the interaction of user identity, preference articulation, and the model's internalized spatial logic of place, rather than a static property.
